A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAFT: Prompt-Agnostic Fine-Tuning. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including material retained under different numbering or placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaMA3-8B/LoRA experiments, prompt-sensitivity measurements, ablations, inference and training times, and prompt-generation costs.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds benchmark evaluations, GRPO comparisons, adversarial-prompt tests, response case studies and prompt-distribution measurements.

M1.justification: The two-stage prompt construction and dynamic SFT algorithm remain essentially unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds an explicit GRPO integration that randomly samples candidate prompts at each reinforcement-learning training step, extending the training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds HumanEval, Xstory_cloze, T-Eval, GSM8K and Geometry3k (Table 2), substantially broadening reported coding, tool-use and mathematical/multimodal coverage. Table 4 adds adversarial/noisy-prompt evaluation. Specific languages evaluated within Xstory_cloze are not documented.

E2.justification: The original Base, User-specified/User, TopAccuracy, BATprompt and ZOPO comparators remain. Figure 7 adds a GRPO comparator on GSM8K. However, Table 2 labels the new mathematical comparisons SFT, whereas Table 7 assigns them to GRPO, limiting precise alignment.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce additional Llama and Qwen configurations, including a vision-language model (Table 7), and GRPO with 10 epochs, 16 generations and learning rate 5e-6 (Table 9). Evaluation adds minimum accuracy across 50 prompts and conditional accuracy on 10 adversarial prompts. The test-prompt description changes from generated prompts to a human/LLM mixture, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds worst-case and adversarial robustness analysis (Table 4), MMD versus training-prompt-count analysis (Figure 9), and three inference-response case studies (Appendix C.2). The existing K/T ablation and prompt-count study remain as Table 5 and Figure 8.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations describing variation across prompts. New result rows retain this reporting practice. Neither version reports training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include HumanEval accuracy of 54.24% for PAFT versus 49.63% for SFT (Table 2), and adversarial HellaSwag accuracy of 84.61% versus 61.26% (Table 4). New figures and case studies add further findings. Original benchmark, timing, ablation and generation-cost values remain unchanged; these additions are not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a domain-adaptation risk bound (Equation 1), an MMD definition and discrepancy-bound proposition, and an RKHS richness assumption with a proof sketch in Appendix A. v1 has no corresponding theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on prompt-robust SFT. v2 expands the claimed first systematic approach to both SFT and RLFT, and adds theoretical support for cross-domain generalization as a main contribution in the abstract and introduction. The original robustness and efficiency claims are retained.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explains generalization through complexity control and alignment between training and test prompt distributions. v2 also interprets adversarial results as resilience to noisy inputs and explicitly clarifies that inference gains concern shorter outputs rather than faster per-token generation. The limitations discussion remains essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies concrete zero-shot and one-shot prompt-generation instructions where v1 provided strategy descriptions and generated examples (Appendix D.1). It also adds GRPO integration instructions, hyperparameters and model–dataset–training mappings (Appendix B.3, Tables 7 and 9). Existing SFT settings and prompt examples are retained.

R1.justification: Positioning broadens from prompt-robust SFT to SFT/RLFT and domain adaptation. Added literature includes GRPO, instruction tuning, newer prompt optimization, and domain-adaptation/MMD foundations. Some earlier citations, including Zhu et al.'s PromptRobust, are removed; the novelty claim now explicitly covers RLFT.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed, with named paragraph headings and a restructured contribution list. A theoretical section is inserted and appendices are reorganized. Author, affiliation and acknowledgement text also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark and robustness tables, model/task mappings, GRPO settings, and T-Eval, GSM8K and MMD figures. Existing displays are retained but several move, including Figure 5 and Algorithm 1; captions and baseline labels are shortened. New boxed templates and response examples expand the appendix displays.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens v1's narrow SFT evaluation and adds useful generation templates and training details. However, Tables 2 and 7 conflict over SFT/GRPO settings, and Appendix A assumes a uniform RKHS norm bound for all 1-Lipschitz functions, which arbitrarily large constant functions violate as written. These issues affect newly emphasized empirical and theoretical contributions, leaving the net quality improvement uncertain.
